answer: AI agent economies resist Sybil attacks by requiring each registrant to solve a sequential time-lock puzzle based on an iterated cipher. Executing this non-parallelizable compute kernel forces an attacker to expend dedicated wall-clock processor time per identity. Consequently, malicious nodes cannot harbor arbitrarily large swarms of counterfeit agents. A primary limitation is that adversaries using specialized ASICs can evaluate the puzzles substantially faster than commodity participants.
